items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good 'what if' geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: rise with real curiosity on every question, say every number with genuine amazement, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. Read 'and said...' with a suspenseful pause, then the twelve-hundred line as a quote. Chars is a cheeky, proud cartoon Kiwi with a strong New Zealand accent, short and indignant. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level throughout. Pronounce 'pavlova' as 'pav-LOH-vuh'.
lines: Narrator
What if New Zealand became Australia's seventh state?
Narrator
Here's the wild part: Australia's constitution still allows it.
Narrator
New Zealand is literally written into it, right next to New South Wales.
Narrator
So what would this new country get?
Narrator
About thirty-three million people... and almost a hundred million sheep.
Narrator
That's about three sheep per person.
Narrator
Plus an economy worth over two trillion dollars.
Narrator
And honestly? They'd barely need a new flag.
Narrator
So why did New Zealand say no?
Narrator
In eighteen ninety, they sat down with Australia to talk about uniting.
Narrator
But one New Zealand delegate pointed at the map and said...
Narrator
twelve hundred miles of ocean are twelve hundred reasons to say no.
Narrator
But Australia's answer was even better.
Narrator
In nineteen oh-one, they united without New Zealand... and left the door open. It's still open.
Narrator
Since nineteen seventy-three, they can live and work in each other's country, as long as they like.
Narrator
So who gets the capital? Canberra... or Wellington?
Chars
[cheeky, proud] And the pavlova is OURS!
Narrator
So, one country or stay two? Because honestly...
